doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Duke Ellington's charm and eccentricities
summary: Jacobs tells stories of Ellington at a birthday party, with his poodle, at Reuben's, and about his sister Ruth.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: No, the spirit of these individuals comes across in their performance for sure, and was Duke Ellington, I never had the pleasure of meeting him. Was he as charming as everyone makes him to be?

Nobody makes him out to be anything that he wasn’t. He had exquisite manners and style. He was absolutely charming. He was the essence of refinement whether he had his dinner or he would talk to a waiter or a busboy, whatever it was he did he did it like an elegant gentleman. He had exquisite vocabulary, expressed himself divinely and nobody really knew Duke Ellington because there were about ten Duke Ellingtons. I never knew which one he was going to bring into work.
Well name a few of the Duke Ellingtons.
Well let’s say Duke Ellington was very complex in the sense that he could adjust himself to whatever situation he was in. I did a party for Arthur Rice’s mother, who was going to

be 80 years old, I worked at the Rainbow Room and Duke Ellington was the artist that was performing with his orchestra. And I said to Mercer, who was part of his band and was very involved in his father’s career, that was Duke’s only son, “Merce, I got a lady that’s having a birthday party, 80 years, when the band breaks does their break let them all come for champagne and cake, it would make her very happy. She’ll be very excited.” And I invited everybody and they all came. And suddenly, who do I see come walking down the steps but Duke Ellington. And I said, “Edward, what are you doing here?” He says, “Well you invited everybody but me.” I said, “Well I didn’t think you’d have any interest in this girl, she’s going to be 80 years old.” He loved women but not 80 years old. He sat and talked to Mrs. Rice for an hour for his entire break. And then for years afterwards she was sending him mass cards, and he would send her flowers. That was one Ellington that amazed me. I couldn’t believe, what could he have in common with an 80- year-old woman. By the same token you could go into a restaurant with Duke and he had a French poodle that Joe Glaser gave him and he loved Davy and he’d have permission to go into the Hickory House with Davy and Davy would sit right next to Edward on the side of his seat and never move. And if Ellington fed him he’d feed him with his hand and the dog was very well behaved. He got into a conversation with the bus boy ‘cause the bus boy’s father raised poodles. And for the rest of the night he didn’t talk to me. Then another time he said to me, “Don’t go home now, wait around I’ll take you for breakfast.” Okay, that was exciting, to go to breakfast with Duke. And he used to love to go to a restaurant called Reuben’s on 58th Street and Fifth Avenue. He had a charge account there. We come down stairs at Rockefeller Center, it’s two o’clock in the morning, and we get a cab. We go from 51st Street over to 58th Street, pull up in front of the restaurant and Duke says, “Pay him.” I paid the cab. We get into the restaurant I said to him, “Edward, why do you have pockets?” He said, “I like to keep my hands in ‘em.” He never walked around with money. He didn’t like to handle money it’s very dirty. I mean he had so many different — and then he couldn’t come in his room, wear anything green, because he was wearing a green tie when he got the news that his mother died. So he was so many, he was so — and then how he treated his sister. His sister Ruth he treated like she was Shirley Temple or Cinderella wrapped all in one. Ruthie was, she’d send mink coats to the club and I’d call Mr. Ellington and I’d say “I have a man who wants $3,400” or something, Ruth’s fur coat. He’d say, “Well give it to the gentleman.” You know I mean it was part of his salary I mean I could give it to him but I wasn’t going to do it unless he said so. I mean he would just do outlandish things. He was absolutely off the wall but delightful.
